summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests JNJ-79635322, a trispecific antibody, in adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma or previously treated AL amyloidosis. The study drug is given as a subcutaneous injection, and how often and for how long it is given is not stated. The main goal is to find the recommended phase 2 dose and schedule that is safe, and to measure safety and tolerability.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1 evalúa JNJ-79635322, un anticuerpo trispecífico, en adultos con mieloma múltiple recidivante o refractario o con amiloidosis AL previamente tratada. El medicamento se administra como inyección subcutánea; la frecuencia y la duración no se indican. El objetivo principal es identificar la dosis recomendada para fase 2 y el esquema seguros, y medir la seguridad y la tolerabilidad.
who_for: Adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma previously treated with a proteasome inhibitor, IMiD and anti-CD38 therapy.
Adults with previously treated AL amyloidosis who are not candidates for available therapy with established benefit.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1 (myeloma participants).
Measurable disease by M-protein, free light chain levels, or extramedullary disease, as defined in the record.
Left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 45% (amyloidosis participants).
not_for: Central nervous system or meningeal involvement of myeloma or amyloidosis.
Any non-AL amyloidosis, including transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis.
Pulmonary compromise needing supplemental oxygen, or serious active infection.
Stroke or seizure within 6 months before the first dose.
Recent anticancer, transplant, or live vaccine treatment within the time windows listed in the record.
